title: Introduce gradient autoscaler and steadyflow credit orchestrator for Dedicated fleets
author: Sofia Alvarez
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet scaling today oscillates under mixed steady and burst workloads leading to elevated 99th percentile latency and unpredictable credit depletion for tenants. This PR implements a gradient-based autoscaler combined with a "steadyflow credit" orchestrator to smooth capacity adjustments and prevent burst credit leakage while preserving short-term burstability. Changes include a new controller that computes continuous gradient estimates of utilization, an adaptive hysteresis curve that maps gradient + level to scale decisions, and a separate lightweight credit manager that maintains a steadyflow budget per-tenant with decay and refill rules. Key outcomes: 1) reduced scale oscillations under synthetic mixed workloads by ~37% in decision frequency; 2) improved 99% tail latency by ~12% at 95th percentile tenant load; 3) steadyflow credits prevent starvation during transient spikes. Implementation notes: core logic added in controllers/fleet/gradient_autoscaler.go and controllers/fleet/steadyflow_orchestrator.go; autoscaler config schema extended under api/v1alpha/autoscaler.yaml; telemetry hooks added to observability/metrics/fleet_telemetry.go and dashboards updated in observability/dashboards/fleet_steadyflow.json. Tests and validation: unit tests for gradient smoothing and credit decay rules, integration harness against perf-lab scenarios that mimic multi-tenant burst patterns, and e2e smoke with dedicated clusters. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag enableGradientAutoscaler=false by default, staged rollout to dedicated fleets via canary annotation fleet.redwood.io/grad-autoscale=canary for 10% of Dedicated pools, monitor the new metrics: fleet.gradient_decision_rate, tenant.steadyflow_balance, fleet.scale_stability_index; automatic rollback if scale decision rate increases by >20% or 99th latency regresses by >5% for 15 minutes. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf bench, [x] docs/upgrade notes, [x] observability dashboards, [x] Linear ticket updated. Related work: builds on prior warm-pool and burst-bank experiments and integrates with existing reservation contracts. Breaking changes: none to API surface; new config fields are additive. Merge: squash and merge after two approvals and successful perf job.

review_comments: Anika Rao: Can you clarify how the gradient smoothing window is chosen? Author: The default window is 60s with exponential decay, configurable via autoscaler.yaml. We added unit tests for several window sizes.
Miles Chen: Observability looks good but add a percentile for decision latency. Author: Added histogram metric fleet.gradient_decision_latency_ms and dashboard tile.
Priya Kapoor: Suggest we simulate tenant reservation interactions. Author: Integration harness updated to include reservation reclaim and warm-pool interactions as a test scenario.
notes_on_validation: Perf runs executed in benchmark-lab: steady-state mixed workload, 3m churn bursts every 30s, observed 37% reduction in scale flips and 12% improvement in 99th percentile generator latency for representative tenants. No regressions on throughput. Monitored tenant.steadyflow_balance to ensure credits do not clamp short bursts.
